title: Private Observability Minimum Pack — Dashboard Wireframes (v0)
body:
Doc intent
- Rough wireframes + panel inventory for the v1 “Private Observability Minimum Pack” dashboards.
- This is not final Grafana JSON. It’s the panel set we believe we can support in air-gapped / customer-run clusters.
- Assumptions: Prometheus + Grafana present (either installed by Redwood charts or customer-provided). Metrics must have bounded label cardinality.

Audience
- Private install platform teams (customers)
- Redwood Support/SRE (day-2 triage)
- Eng owners instrumenting runtime + control plane

Status / what changed recently
- 2025-06-04: added explicit “What’s broken?” panels at top of each dashboard; tightened naming/label proposals to avoid model/route explosion; clarified what panels are optional for v1.

Dashboard taxonomy proposal
Folder: “Redwood Private (Minimum)” (top-level Grafana folder)
Dashboards:
1) Runtime Overview (Serving)
2) Runtime — GPU & Capacity
3) Runtime — Queueing / Batching / KV Cache
4) Control Plane Health
5) API Gateway & Routing
6) Installer / Upgrade Controller
7) Infra Dependencies (optional/minimal): Prometheus scrape health + K8s basics (if we ship it)

Naming conventions (proposals)
- Dashboard titles start with area: “Runtime — …” or “Control Plane — …”
- Panel titles are action-oriented and short; include units.
- For Private, prefer “deployment” and “namespace” over high-cardinality labels like “tenant_id”, “route”, “prompt_id”.
- If a panel *must* break down by model, limit to “model_family” (e.g., llama3, mistral) or “model_alias” (customer-defined stable alias) rather than full version strings.

Global variables (templating)
- $cluster (string; might be constant in Private but keep for compatibility)
- $namespace (default: redwood-system)
- $deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private) — may not exist in Private; only include if it’s cheap
- $service (runtime/control-plane components)
- $instance / $pod (only used in “drill down” dashboards)
- $gpu_node (node label)

Open questions (need decisions)
1) Do we ship “Infra Dependencies” dashboard, or rely on kube-prometheus-stack defaults? Support wants at least scrape/TSDB health panels, but Product is wary of scope.
2) “Model” breakdown: allowed labels in Private? Proposed: model_alias only (bounded list), no raw model_id.
3) “Route” breakdown: allowed? Proposed: route_class (e.g., chat, embeddings, rerank) rather than route_name.
4) Token-level panels: can we compute “tokens/sec” reliably in Private across all runtimes? If not, keep panel optional.
5) Tracing: likely out-of-scope v1; do we include empty placeholders linking to docs?


DASHBOARD 1: Runtime Overview (Serving)
Goal: single pane of glass for oncall to answer “is inference working, is it slow, is it saturating, what changed?”

Layout sketch
Row 0 (top): “What’s broken?” (high-signal)
Row 1: Golden signals (R/E/L/S)
Row 2: Throughput & tokens
Row 3: Errors by class
Row 4: Resource saturation summary
Row 5: Recent deploy/events

Panels (proposed)
A. What’s broken? (stat panels)
- Request success rate (5m) (stat; green/yellow/red thresholds)
- Error rate (5m) (stat)
- p95 latency (5m) (stat)
- Active incidents: runtime pods crashlooping (stat count)
- Prometheus scrape up for runtime targets (stat)

B. Golden signals (timeseries)
- RPS (requests/sec) — total
- Error rate (%) — total
- Latency p50/p95/p99 (ms)
- Saturation proxy (see below; may be GPU util or queueing)

C. Throughput
- Tokens/sec (generated) — total (if available)
- Tokens/request distribution (p50/p95)
- Streaming vs non-streaming request rate (if metric exists; optional)

D. Errors
- 5xx rate by error_class (timeout, upstream, runtime_error, overload)
- 4xx rate by category (auth, rate_limit, invalid_request) (optional; may be gateway-owned)
- Top 10 error messages (table) — careful: text cardinality. Prefer error_code not raw strings.

E. Saturation / capacity
- GPU utilization avg (or SM occupancy) (timeseries)
- GPU memory used / total (timeseries)
- Runtime queue depth (timeseries)
- Batch size (avg/p95) (timeseries)

F. Deploy / events
- Pod restarts (bar chart)
- Rollout status (desired vs available replicas)
- Config/policy version applied (if exported) (annotation/event)

Queries / metric dependencies (placeholders)
- redwood_runtime_requests_total{status=…}
- redwood_runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket
- redwood_runtime_queue_depth
- redwood_runtime_tokens_generated_total (optional)
- nvidia_dcgm_gpu_utilization (or exporter equivalent)
- kube_deployment_status_replicas_available

Notes
- “Saturation” definition: do not invent a single saturation % if we don’t have solid semantics. Use GPU util + queue depth as primary.


DASHBOARD 2: Runtime — GPU & Capacity
Goal: answer “are we running out of GPU capacity; is this node sick; are we memory bound?”

Layout sketch
Row 0: Fleet summary stats
Row 1: Per-node GPU utilization + memory
Row 2: OOM / throttling / evictions
Row 3: GPU errors (Xid, ECC)
Row 4: Pod placement & imbalance

Panels
A. Fleet summary
- # GPUs (detected) (stat)
- % GPUs > 90% util (stat)
- % GPUs > 90% memory (stat)
- Runtime pods per GPU (stat) (if we can compute)

B. Utilization
- GPU util by node (heatmap)
- GPU memory used by node (heatmap)
- GPU power / thermal throttling flags (table; optional, hardware dependent)

C. OOM / restarts
- Runtime container OOM kills (timeseries)
- Restarts by pod (table)
- GPU memory fragmentation proxy (?) (likely out-of-scope)

D. GPU health
- Xid error count by node (timeseries/table)
- ECC errors (if available)

E. Placement/imbalance
- Runtime requests/sec by pod (topk) (to detect hot pod)
- GPU util variance across nodes (single stat; optional)

Label constraints (cardinality)
- Node name is bounded by cluster size.
- Avoid exposing pod UID labels if possible.


DASHBOARD 3: Runtime — Queueing / Batching / KV Cache
Goal: explain latency: is it queueing? batching too aggressive? cache ineffective?

Layout sketch
Row 0: queue/latency correlation
Row 1: queue depth + time in queue
Row 2: batching behavior
Row 3: KV cache and context reuse
Row 4: backpressure + overload controls

Panels
A. Queue vs latency
- Latency p95 vs queue depth (two-axis timeseries)

B. Queue metrics
- Queue depth (avg/p95/max)
- Time in queue (p50/p95) (if we instrument)
- Dropped/Rejected requests due to overload (rate)

C. Batching metrics
- Batch size distribution (histogram)
- Batch wait time (ms)
- Continuous batching “active batches” (gauge)

D. KV cache
- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV) (stat + timeseries)
- Cache bytes used (timeseries)
- Cache evictions (rate)

E. Backpressure
- Concurrency limit reached events (rate)
- Circuit breaker / fallback activation count (rate) (if Private includes fallback behavior)

Open instrumentation gaps
- “Time in queue” is not consistently emitted today in Private builds.
- KV cache: definitions differ by runtime version; need stable metric names or a migration plan.


DASHBOARD 4: Control Plane Health
Goal: ensure private control plane is healthy (config/policy, auth/RBAC integration points, model registry connectivity).

Layout sketch
Row 0: top health checks
Row 1: service SLO-ish golden signals
Row 2: dependency health (DB, registry, external IDP)
Row 3: work queues / controllers

Panels
A. Health checks
- Control plane API availability (up / 5xx)
- Policy engine errors (rate)
- Auth failures (rate) (careful: security-sensitive; only counts)

B. Latency + errors by service
- p95 latency per control plane service (table)
- Error rate per service (table)

C. Dependencies
- DB connection pool saturation (if available)
- Model registry sync success/failure (rate)
- External IDP (OIDC) token validation failures (rate)

D. Controllers
- Reconciliation loop duration (p95)
- Reconcile errors (rate)
- Queue depth (if controller-runtime exposes)


DASHBOARD 5: API Gateway & Routing
Goal: find issues at the edge: auth, rate limiting, routing, upstream selection.

Panels
- Incoming RPS by route_class (chat/embeddings/rerank) (no raw route names)
- 4xx vs 5xx rate
- Request size (bytes) p95 (optional; may not exist)
- Upstream selection counts (by upstream type: runtime pool A/B, fallback) (optional)
- Rate limit throttles (rate)
- TLS handshake / upstream connect errors (rate)

Open question
- Where does gateway live in Private topology? If customer brings their own gateway, we might only expose Redwood “API service” metrics.


DASHBOARD 6: Installer / Upgrade Controller
Goal: support and customer ops can verify upgrades, detect stuck migrations, understand drift.

Panels
- Current installed version (stat; from installer controller)
- Last upgrade time + status (table)
- Failed preflight checks count (table)
- Reconcile errors (rate)
- Helm release status (if available) (table)
- Artifact bundle verification status (air-gap) (stat; optional)


DASHBOARD 7 (OPTIONAL): Infra Dependencies (minimal)
Only if we decide to ship. Otherwise, link to kube-prometheus-stack dashboards.

Panels
- Prometheus targets up (by job)
- TSDB head series + churn (cardinality red flags)
- Prometheus scrape duration / sample ingestion rate
- Grafana datasource health (if measurable)


Panel ordering “rules” (to keep dashboards consistent)
- Always start with: Availability, Errors, Latency, Saturation.
- Then: explainers (queueing/batching/cache) or infra (gpu/memory).
- Drilldowns at bottom.

Design notes for Private constraints
- Air-gapped packaging: dashboards must be shipped as files in the bundle (no remote imports).
- Avoid dashboard dependencies on external plugins.
- Prefer recording rules for expensive aggregations. Don’t ship dashboards that require wide label joins.
- Every dashboard should work with 7-day retention (default) and 15s-30s scrape interval.

Cardinality guardrails (draft)
- Disallowed / strongly discouraged labels in Private dashboards:
  - request_id, prompt_id, user_id, raw tenant_id, raw route_name, raw model_id (full SHA/version)
- Allowed with constraints:
  - tenant_tier (small enum), model_alias (bounded), route_class (bounded), region (bounded), namespace, pod (for drilldown only)

Runbook integration (request from oncall)
- Each dashboard should have a top “Runbook” link panel with:
  - what this dashboard is for
  - first 3 checks
  - link to Confluence runbook

TODOs / next steps
- Convert wireframes into Grafana JSON skeletons (Sergio/Chloe)
- Confirm exact metric names post ENG-19143 (Thomas/Nadia)
- Add recording rules proposals for heavy queries (Logan)
- Validate dashboards in staging private cluster + tune defaults (Rafael)

Appendix: candidate metric names (strawman, not final)
- redwood_runtime_requests_total{status_class="2xx|4xx|5xx", route_class="chat|embeddings|rerank", model_alias="…"}
- redwood_runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route_class="…"}
- redwood_runtime_queue_depth{queue="ingress"}
- redwood_runtime_queue_time_seconds_bucket
- redwood_runtime_batch_size_bucket
- redwood_runtime_kv_cache_hit_total / redwood_runtime_kv_cache_miss_total
- redwood_controlplane_http_requests_total{service="policy|registry|auth|api"}
- redwood_installer_reconcile_errors_total

Non-goals for v1 dashboards (explicit)
- Per-tenant dashboards
- Full trace waterfall views
- Prompt/content inspection
- Customer-specific business KPIs
